what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the tools in tools/decide-with-a-method: decisions a person's AI makes with a method, kept as the person's own decision records.

payload.label: Bring back my similar decisions
payload.job: When I am about to decide something, show what I decided in similar decisions before, what came next and how each turned out
payload.description: Reads the person's own decision records. The newest ones are weighed by the words their goals share with the named decision's goal, plus a point for the same method (read-data/decide-with-a-method.json `similar`). The closest are kept, closest first, limit of them (10 when not given, never more than 50). Each comes back with its goal, its method, the option it chose, its next action, its status (from its own current evidence) and its observed and reported results. Only those few are read whole, and nothing leaves the person's account.

decision_id.description: The decision about to be made

payload.label: Start a decision with my method
payload.job: Start a decision my AI will make with my method: what is being decided, the facts and constraints, and the options only if I already hold them
payload.description: Opens a decision in the person's own records from a source_id (the same source always opens the same decision; the same input again is that decision, different input is refused), its goal, its evidence ({ref, claim}, each ref unique: the facts and every non-negotiable constraint) and, only when the caller already holds them, at least two options ({id, label}); with no options the method's own steps generate the candidates and rule them out, and what the rule-out step leaves standing are the options, under the method named or the person's default (their Methods list). The decision keeps the exact method it was opened with. Returns case_id and the first question.

source_id.description: Unique text naming where this decision comes from

method.description: A method id from the person's methods

record_model._what: The record kinds, indexes and links this tool keeps (moved unchanged from trillion-rust's one record model: src/record_model_policy/record-model.json, src/record_indexes/record-indexes.json, product/lists.json field_kinds and product/record-sharing.json links).

payload.label: Answer a decision's question
payload.job: Answer the question my method is asking about a decision, with each of its checks; change an answer I gave before with its reason, which reopens a decided decision; confirm an answer that must be asked again, or add the judge's verdicts to an answer I have; or bring in an answer from another of my decisions
payload.description: Answers the decision's current question (step_id) with answer as its answer_schema says: every field, every check handled (how) or, where allowed, not applying (because), each citing the decision's evidence refs or the person's current pursuit ids. verdicts are your judge's, beside the answer, one for every check; an answer with fewer is refused (verdicts_missing) and the step stays unanswered; a refusal that rests on the answer or an evidence ref and names words of its check refuses the answer. Out of turn is refused; the same answer again replays. revise changes an answer already given: it names because (why, in a few words) and keeps the old version, and every later answer of the decision is marked to be asked again, so the next question is the earliest of them. On a decided decision, revise reopens it: the decision it had moves to decision_history, marked reopened with its reason and when, and the decision must be made again with tool:make-the-decision. confirm keeps a re-asked answer unchanged; with verdicts it adds them to an answered step, open or decided, as a new version with the same answer, each verdict kept with when it came in; a verdict already kept is never changed, and a decided decision stays decided. from, instead of answer, brings in another of the person's decisions' answer to the same step as it stood (its version, or the current one), with the evidence it cites, and checks it as a typed answer. After a failed result, revise changes the answer and the decision stands until a new one is made. Keeps the answer as its own step record and returns the next question.

answer.description: The answer as the question's answer_schema says; not sent with from or with confirm

verdicts.description: Your judge's verdicts on this step's checks, as the question's `verdicts` words say: each { check, meets, rests_on, missing?, graded_by }; with confirm, only the checks the step has no verdict for yet are added

usage.description: What answering cost, as you count it (model calls, tokens, seconds, a model name)

from.description: Bring in another of the person's decisions' answer to this step as it stood instead of sending answer

version.description: The version of that answer; the current one when left out

revise.description: Changes an answer already given: why it changes, in a few words; by names who changed it. On a decided decision it reopens the decision

because.description: Why the answer changes, in words; kept on the reopened decision too

by.description: Who changed it, when not the calling AI

confirm.description: Confirms a re-asked answer unchanged, or, with verdicts, adds them to an answered step as a new version of the same answer; sent alone or with verdicts (no answer, from or revise)

payload.label: See my decisions
payload.job: Show my decisions, what I am working toward, my plans and what has helped me decide
payload.description: Reads your own rows and answers the Decisions screen: your newest decisions (at most 100) as summaries with the pursuits each cites, where each stands and how far it has got (decided, next action carried out, result checked); your current pursuits as the tree they nest into (from your record-scope choice rows); your newest plans; and what has helped you (which questions changed your answers and how those decisions turned out). With native_collection_page it answers one bounded page instead: the facts what helped is counted from (helped_items, your method check questions and your AIs' recorded work), collection_coverage saying whether more decisions, pursuits or plans exist, and next_before to send as before for the next page. access and allowance are what your place reports: when your access limits deciding and does not keep decisions, the answer is free with nothing listed; none reported is no limit. metadata_only answers only access, allowance and the words for no pursuits, and reads no row. It changes nothing.

metadata_only.description: Answer only access, allowance and the no-pursuits words; read no row

native_collection_page.description: One bounded page with its coverage, instead of the whole what-helped view

before.description: The next_before an earlier page answered: the page starts below this created_at

access.description: What your place reports: { capabilities: [names], limits?: { [access]: [{ count, per }] } }
